rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers just told investors their business will be larger and more profitable by 2027 than they previously expected — that's a good sign for anyone holding the stock for the long term. The stock currently trades as if the company will barely grow at all (about 4% per year), which
risks: Upgraded guidance increases the bar management must clear; a future miss against a raised target would be more damaging to credibility than missing a conservative baseline.
Teva product expansion, if funded with meaningful marketing spend, could dilute management attention and capital away from HOKA and UGG without commensurate return.
Revenue milestone achieved without margin detail creates a temporary information gap — if Q1 margins compressed to drive volume, the quality of this milestone would be lower than it appears.
A $1B Q1 raises the base for year-over-year comparisons in future periods, increasing the risk of optically weak growth rates even if absolute dollar growth continues.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Meta just reported a quarter that disappointed Wall Street — earnings came in below expectations and the company's forward guidance wasn't encouraging, sending the stock down about 10%. However, we don't yet have the actual numbers from the earnings release, so we can't tell whet
risks: Capex guidance may have been raised materially, potentially pushing FCF inflection further into the future and compressing near-term free cash flow yield.
If guidance disappointment reflects softening advertiser demand rather than internal execution issues, macro-driven ad spend deceleration could persist across multiple quarters.
Market narrative around 'barely passable' execution could affect advertiser confidence or talent retention if it hardens into a sustained perception of strategic drift.

JV terms may include off-balance-sheet obligations (minimum purchase commitments, guaranteed returns to BlackRock) that replicate the economic burden of direct ownership without the transparency of a standard capex line.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: A rumor circulating on a retail stock-discussion platform claims Amazon quietly put its Nova AI models on the back burner before its next earnings report. This could mean Amazon is being more disciplined about where it spends its AI budget — which would actually be good for cash
risks: If Amazon is pulling back from first-party frontier AI model development, it risks ceding AI-native workload acquisition to Azure (OpenAI) and Google Cloud (Gemini), potentially slowing AWS's ability to capture net-new AI spending in the medium term.

The report's pre-earnings timing could indicate a deliberate or inadvertent information leak, which itself carries a reputational and regulatory risk if material non-public information was involved — though this is speculative.
Trainium adoption requires customers to retool AI workflows for non-Nvidia hardware; slower-than-expected developer uptake could limit the competitive moat benefit.
Heavy capex for robotic warehouses and AI chip infrastructure keeps capital intensity elevated; if utilization ramps slowly, ROIC temporarily compresses before the efficiency gains materialize.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: After the European Union fined Google for antitrust violations related to its dominant search position, competing companies are now suing Google for damages in civil courts, with total claims potentially reaching $10 billion. For a company generating over $70 billion in free cash
risks: Follow-on civil suits in the EU could aggregate to $10B in damages, representing a meaningful but absorbable cash outflow over multiple years.
A successful plaintiff recovery could embolden further copycat suits in other jurisdictions, increasing the total regulatory overhang.
Courts adjudicating civil claims could impose behavioral remedies beyond what the original EC fine required, potentially restricting distribution agreements that underpin Search's default placement.
Capex acceleration may be outpacing near-term AI revenue generation, compressing FCF returns below historical norms for longer than the market or thesis assumes.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: Reports say NVIDIA may be helping to finance OpenAI's purchase of NVIDIA hardware — essentially lending money to a customer to buy your own products. On one hand, this shows just how central NVIDIA is to the AI world: the most important AI company apparently wants NVIDIA's chips
risks: Vendor financing of GPU purchases, if confirmed and material, introduces credit concentration risk to NVIDIA's balance sheet tied to OpenAI's financial health.
A pattern of vendor-financed demand would raise questions about whether AI infrastructure capex is as organically robust as current revenue growth implies.
Reputational and regulatory risk if the financing arrangement is structured in a way that regulators view as anticompetitive or as a mechanism to lock OpenAI into NVIDIA exclusively.

If Google's chip achieves commercial-scale deployment with verified 10x inference cost reduction, it could accelerate hyperscaler substitution of NVIDIA GPUs for inference workloads, compressing both volumes and ASPs in the fastest-growing AI compute segment.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM's stock jumped about 5% in one day, but there was no news behind it — no earnings, no announcement, nothing. This kind of move happens in the market and doesn't tell us anything about whether IBM's business is getting better or worse. The company's value hasn't changed; we're
risks: Undisclosed purchase price prevents assessment of whether IBM deployed capital at a value-destructive valuation — will need disclosure to clear the kill criterion check on value-destructive acquisitions.

Quantum computing timelines are highly uncertain; if IBM escalates investment in quantum at the expense of software and hybrid cloud execution, it could distract management attention from the core thesis drivers.

Mid-year revenue guidance cut signals either Consulting cyclical weakness or Software deceleration — the latter would directly trigger thesis kill criteria and requires urgent segment-level verification.

Net debt/EBITDA of 3.47x already exceeds our 2.5x threshold; the Confluent acquisition and potential HRL purchase price will likely push leverage higher before it improves, reducing financial flexibility.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: Microsoft just reported its best Azure result ever—the cloud business crossed $100 billion in annual revenue, driven largely by companies paying to run AI workloads on Microsoft's infrastructure. That's the single biggest validation yet that Microsoft's bet on AI is paying off, n
risks: SaaS commoditization of AI features: competitive pressure (OpenAI direct, Google Gemini, Anthropic enterprise) could force Microsoft to bundle Copilot into base M365 pricing rather than sustaining $30/seat uplift, converting a margin-accretive AI monetization story into a defensive retention play.

FCF compression from AI capex may be longer-duration than the market expects if data center build cycles extend 3-5 years before meaningful depreciation flows through, pressuring near-term shareholder returns relative to earnings.

Azure at $100B creates a higher base from which percentage growth rates will mechanically decelerate, potentially disappointing growth-dependent valuation multiples even if absolute dollar growth remains strong.
Lower-cost AI security SKU could cannibalize premium Security Copilot tiers if positioning is not cleanly differentiated, compressing segment ARPU.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Two news articles are essentially saying 'Palantir reports earnings on August 3 and analysts are watching closely.' There is no new information about the actual business — no sales data, no customer numbers, no profit figures. The reason this matters at all is context: Palantir h
risks: Market expectations for a 12th consecutive quarter of revenue acceleration are now explicitly elevated; a deceleration — even a modest one — could trigger outsized price volatility disproportionate to the actual business impact.
The August 3 earnings date compresses the window for position-sizing decisions ahead of a high-expectation print at a ~138x trailing P/E.
Stock trading at ~60x forward earnings and ~$315B market cap creates a high execution bar where any future guidance miss could trigger a severe de-rating, irrespective of underlying business quality.
Without segment detail, there is a non-trivial risk that the beat is government-contract-timing-driven rather than commercial AIP adoption, which would not validate the core long-term thesis driver.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify's stock jumped about 8% today, but there was no news behind it — no earnings, no product announcement, no strategic update. The business itself is unchanged. Shopify is a genuinely excellent company with strong competitive advantages, but the stock already trades at a ver
risks: DoorDash partnership creates a dependency on a third-party logistics network; if DoorDash changes pricing, availability, or terms, merchants enabled through this channel could face disruption with limited Shopify recourse.

Analyst downgrade, even if valuation-driven, can accelerate institutional selling and increase short-term price volatility, which matters only if Shopify needs to issue equity or if management credibility becomes tied to share price performance.
Dependency on DoorDash's own network reliability and pricing could expose Shopify merchants to service disruptions or cost pass-throughs outside Shopify's control.

If DoorDash deteriorates as a business or changes its partner economics, Shopify merchants relying on this integration could be disrupted, potentially creating merchant dissatisfaction attributed to the Shopify platform.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: UnitedHealth just reported better-than-expected profits and raised its earnings outlook for the year, which is a good sign that management is running the business well right now. At the same time, the federal government announced it will stop subsidizing a key part of Medicare dr
risks: Federal removal of Medicare drug plan subsidy creates a structural cost shift onto Part D plan sponsors, compressing pharmacy segment margins from 2026 onward.
Medicare drug plan premium increases may drive membership attrition in price-sensitive low-income cohorts, reducing Optum pharmacy and UHC government segment volumes.
Policy direction under the current administration appears incrementally hostile to Medicare subsidy structures, raising the probability of further reimbursement changes beyond this single action.

If the article's unnamed risk relates to Medicare Advantage rate pressure or elevated MCR persistence, that would represent a material thesis risk — but content must be reviewed before concluding this.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: ASTS stock fell about 6% today, but nothing actually happened to the business. For a company that is still building its satellite network and has almost no revenue yet, this kind of daily price swing is completely normal. The real questions — are the satellites getting built and
risks: Launch vehicle failure or anomaly on August 5 would simultaneously destroy three BlueBird satellites and set back the commercial timeline by 12+ months, directly triggering the kill criterion around repeated execution delays.
On-orbit performance of BlueBird generation satellites remains unproven at commercial scale — even a successful launch leaves activation, calibration, and service quality risk outstanding.
Starlink may be accelerating commercial D2D deployment through MNO channels, potentially pre-empting ASTS's distribution advantage before ASTS achieves meaningful commercial scale.
Analyst skepticism about timing could impair ASTS's ability to raise capital on favorable terms, as equity financing remains critical to survival and is sentiment-dependent.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Tesla just reported earnings that disappointed investors enough to send the stock down about 15% over six days. The company's profit margins on cars have been squeezed for two years — from about 25 cents of gross profit per dollar of revenue down to about 18 cents — and this quar
risks: The magnitude of the implied value destruction ($25B) suggests guidance for 2025 or beyond may have been cut, introducing risk that consensus earnings estimates are still too high and further multiple compression is possible.
A six-day losing streak to multi-year lows increases the risk of forced selling by momentum and index-rebalancing flows, adding near-term price volatility unrelated to fundamentals.

If the earnings miss is partly attributable to Elon Musk's attention being diverted to political/governmental roles (DOGE, etc.), key-person execution risk — already a known risk — becomes more acute.

Stock-based compensation running at ~$4.6B annualized pace in 2026 represents a structural per-share dilution headwind not previously modeled at this magnitude, particularly tied to Musk's new performance grant.
